html:
Yerba mate is a drink made from the dried leaves of a holly tree native to Paraguay and nearby lands. The Guarani drank it, and Spanish settlers in Asunción took it up in the 1500s.

The leaves are steeped in hot water in a gourd and sipped through a metal straw, passed from hand to hand. In Paraguay it is also drunk cold as tereré, listed by UNESCO in 2020. For centuries leaves were gathered from wild trees by forced labour. The Jesuit missions learned to grow the tree from seed and ran large plantations, and mate was the region's chief export.

Mate became the everyday drink of the whole Río de la Plata, from the gauchos of the pampas to the cafés of Buenos Aires and Uruguay. It is drunk there as tea or coffee is elsewhere.
